newsitem.title: UK: UK/Cont crude oil Aframax tankers stay tight, firm.
newsitem.headline: UK/Cont crude oil Aframax tankers stay tight, firm.

text.p: Chartering rates for 80,000 tonne Aframax crude oil tankers remained firm on Monday at Friday's sky-high levels as a shortage of vessels continued to pressure the market, shipbrokers said.
But holidays in a number of countries stifled trade.
Mobil's fixture of the 80,000 tonne Hanne Knutsen and an Alandia ship, both at W155, broadly represented the market, brokers said.
"There is an end-month squeeze and there are hardly any ships," one said, assessing the prompt market at W150-155.
But rates into June were expected to weaken.
Maintenance programmes at some North Sea fields also meant enquiry was likely to slacken.
Brokers said high prices in northwest Europe, however, were not having a knock-on effect in the Med, where similarly sized vessels were going for W105.
"You do get a few drifters but by and large the players stick to their own regions, he said. Another player in the Med assessed Aframax rates at W102.5-W105.
He said that Petrogal's fixture of a 130,000 tonner at W85 was around 10 points below the market, because it was an old ship.
But he added: "Today has been absolutely quiet because of the holiday."

Mideast/east voyages for Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) were also stable at around W60-65, although Caribs/USAC routes for 70,000 tonne vessels were slightly firmer again, as evidenced by Lyondell's fixture of the 70,000 tonne Velez Blanco for this route at W200.
